slot.brief: Determinant whose entries are row sums/column expressions; show it equals a product of linear factors using row/column operations.

verdicts.working: Subtract row 1 from row 2 and row 2 from row 3. The resulting matrix is upper triangular with diagonal entries \(a+b,e,g\), so its determinant is \((a+b)eg\).

working:
Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-R_2$, then $R_2\leftarrow R_2-R_1$: $\begin{vmatrix}a+b&b+c&c+d\\0&e&f\\0&0&g\end{vmatrix}=(a+b)eg$.

Independent check: Subtract row 1 from row 2 and row 2 from row 3. The resulting matrix is upper triangular with diagonal entries \(a+b,e,g\), so its determinant is \((a+b)eg\).
solution:
Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-R_2$, then $R_2\leftarrow R_2-R_1$; these row operations preserve the determinant.
$$\begin{vmatrix}a+b&b+c&c+d\\0&e&f\\0&0&g\end{vmatrix}=(a+b)eg$$

draft.distractor_notes: B: uses the wrong entry in the second pivot; C: uses the wrong entry in the third pivot; D: incorrectly changes the first diagonal entry.
